parameters.content:
# Track Greenhouse job changes with Apify and saved snapshots

## Who is this for?

Automation builders maintaining a job feed for a known list of companies using Greenhouse. This workflow keeps the previous observation so you can compare listing metadata without manually copying a snapshot.

## How it works

Run the workflow manually. It checks 1–20 boards with Greenhouse Watchlist Export, validates completion and saves the new snapshot in a dedicated Apify key-value store. The next execution compares against that history and returns observed changes. The first run is a baseline, not proof that every job is new.

An unfinished run is resumed on the next execution. If a start response is lost, the workflow stops for inspection instead of starting another run automatically.

## Setup and requirements

1. Use n8n and an Apify account. Add one Header Auth credential (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) to every HTTP node.
2. Edit **Watchlist settings**: board slugs, dedicated store name and the single-writer confirmation.
3. Run the whole workflow twice, sequentially. Check **Results** for saved history and `baseline: false` on the second run.

The template is free; the required [Apify Actor](https://apify.com/downy_sublimity/greenhouse-watchlist-export) currently costs **US$0.05 per completed watchlist**, including unchanged/empty checks. Separate n8n hosting and platform/storage costs may apply.

Use one writer per store. No schedule or notifications are included. A changed board list needs a new store and baseline. Tested with n8n 2.42.6; setup and recovery instructions are included in the workflow notes.

## 1. Configure and recover history
Select your Header Auth credential in every HTTP node. In Watchlist settings, choose board slugs and a dedicated store. Set singleWriterConfirmed=true only when one workflow and one execution will write this store.

The default is deliberately false. An existing pending run is retrieved without a new POST. Do not erase STATE to clear an error.

## 2. Start once or resume
The workflow saves and reads back the start intent before calling the Actor. A missing response leaves a pending state for inspection. Never retry the POST node alone.

The status request waits for up to 60 seconds; there is no automatic polling loop. If a run is still working, execute the whole workflow later to retrieve it. For failed runs or an unknown start, follow the Recover interrupted checks note below.

## 3. Validate, save and inspect Results
History advances only after a successful complete run, confirmed completion receipt, matching snapshot and complete change file. A partial or uncertain result preserves the previous snapshot.

Results includes the run link, counts and changes. Baseline events are first observations; a disappearance is confirmed after two valid absences and does not prove that a role was filled.

## Recovery without duplicate starts
These instructions are included here so no external setup file is required.

**Known pendingRunId:** run the whole workflow later to retrieve that same run. If still working, wait. Never retry the POST node alone.

**Pending state without an ID:** the start may have reached Apify even if its response was lost. In Apify Runs, inspect this Actor around STATE.startedAt and compare the exact board list and input. Back up STATE. Only after uniquely identifying the run may an operator record its ID as pendingRunId, preserving every other field, then rerun the whole workflow. If uncertain, stop.

**Failed or aborted run:** inspect the run and billing first. After confirming it is terminal, an operator can deliberately restore status=ready, preserve snapshot and lastRunId, and remove pending fields. This permits a new paid check. Do not resurrect the run or adopt partial outputs.

**Unknown billing:** inspect Apify charging records before any further payment action. Do not retry a charge.

**Save acknowledgement lost:** inspect STATE. A ready state with the expected lastRunId means history was saved. Never replace it with an older snapshot or erase history to clear an error.

Keep the named store private. Review n8n execution retention. This workflow has no distributed lock; one writer and one execution per store is mandatory.
